info.name: Shoof API
info.description:
Full endpoint coverage for Shoof's two ASP.NET Core APIs plus the public Portal surface.

## APIs
- **Restaurant API** ({{restaurantBaseUrl}}) -- tenant-scoped restaurant-admin surface (Shoof.Api.Restaurant). Requires Bearer JWT + X-Api-Key + X-Tenant-Id.
- **SuperAdmin API** ({{superAdminBaseUrl}}) -- platform-operator, cross-tenant surface (Shoof.Api.SuperAdmin). Requires Bearer JWT only.
- **Portal API** -- public, anonymous, API-key-only customer menu (served from the Restaurant API host, but no JWT/tenant header at all).

## Getting started
1. Run **SuperAdmin API > Auth > Login** first -- support@lambdor.com is pre-seeded with every permission (see SuperAdminPermissionSeeder), so this always works against a fresh DB.
   It is the primary SuperAdmin and must change its seed password first: run **SuperAdmin API > Account > Change Password**, then set {{superAdminPassword}} to the new one (every other call returns 403 "Password change required." until then). The same applies to any admin created by someone else.
2. Run **SuperAdmin API > Currencies > Create**, then **Model Archetypes > Create**, then **Tenants > Create** (captures {{tenantId}}/{{tenantSlug}}), then **Restaurants > Create** (captures {{restaurantId}}).
3. **There is no bootstrap endpoint for the first AdminUser of a tenant.** Nothing in this collection can create it, because AdminUsers.Create itself requires an already-authenticated admin. Seed one directly (e.g. the same way the test suite's `IntegrationTestFixture.SeedAdminUserAsync` does, via `UserManager<AdminUser>.CreateAsync` against the dev DB), then set {{adminEmail}}/{{adminPassword}} to match before running **Restaurant API > Auth > Login**.
4. Once logged in as that seeded admin, everything else in the Restaurant API folder works normally -- including creating further AdminUsers and Roles through the API itself from there on.
5. Grant that admin's role permissions via **Restaurant API > Roles > Create/Update** (permissions list) and assign the role via **Admin Users > Create/Update** (roles list) before expecting a 403 to go away on a permission-gated endpoint.

## Auth token lifetime
JWTs expire after 60 minutes (Jwt:MinutesExpires). Re-run the relevant Login request, or use the Auth > Refresh Token request with the stored refresh token, if requests start failing with 401.

item.description:
Read + generate only -- QR codes are never edited or deleted. tableId null = the restaurant's general QR; set = a specific table's QR.

targetUrl is the full absolute menu URL the QR encodes: https://{slug}.{Portal:BaseDomain}/menu/{restaurantId}[/table/{tableId}] (e.g. https://pizzahut.shoof.lambdor.com/menu/...), so a scanned QR opens the menu directly. imageUrl is the rendered PNG, a public stored file.

Generating is idempotent: POSTing the same restaurantId+tableId again returns the same QR (same id); the PNG is redrawn only when targetUrl changed (e.g. after Portal:BaseDomain changed). Both Generate requests check targetUrl and save the PNG's path in storedFilePath, so the Files folder can fetch it.

For a B2B partner (e.g. BeeOrder) that runs its own app and never touches the Portal or the admin dashboard -- its own dedicated API project (Shoof.Api.Integration), authenticated purely by possessing the raw ApiKey value (see SuperAdmin API > Api Keys > Create's plainTextKey response, set it as {{integrationApiKey}}), not a JWT. No permissions/roles involved: the key resolves the caller's TenantId directly, and the existing tenant query filters are what keep one partner off another tenant's data. Restaurant creation is self-service (no SuperAdmin approval step) and forces TenantId to the caller's own tenant server-side regardless of what the request body claims. Rate-limited per key (see SuperAdmin API > Api Keys > rateLimitPerMinute).
